confirmed_events.summary: The seed workstation resolved auth-queue-sync.net, a rare domain mapped to a shared hosting IP, before the alert.
Seed JA4 alert observed an unusual TLS session to auth-queue-sync.net on shared infrastructure.
The seed workstation reconnected to the same auth-queue-sync.net endpoint after the seed alert.
A second short TLS session from ws-legal-03 reused the same domain and JA4-adjacent shared hosting path.
Endpoint coverage for ws-legal-03 did not include command-line telemetry during the relevant window.
A second workstation contacted cdn-auth-queue.net on the same shared IP, but only through one weak network signal.
The second workstation resolved a sibling domain pointing to the same shared infrastructure.
The same workstation also used a sanctioned identity-cache vendor domain on the shared hosting IP.
A legal-document review workstation touched the same IP through a different business SaaS domain, suggesting shared infrastructure.
Passive infrastructure context showed the IP hosted multiple unrelated customer domains during the same week.
An approved SSO browser extension update on ws-legal-03 overlapped the first suspicious TLS session.
Normal Microsoft identity traffic from ws-legal-03 appeared in the same SSO workflow window.
The seed workstation later resolved a second rare queue-themed domain, but it did not share the seed IP.
A single TLS connection to the second queue-themed domain remained an unresolved follow-on indicator without host corroboration.
EDR coverage for ws-legal-09 did not include command-line telemetry in this window, limiting scope confirmation.
